title: Publish a concise specification and interoperability identifiers

state.decision_rationale: Accepted as a normative v4 specification and preferred .mktctx extension; text/x-mktctx is documented only as provisional and unregistered.

provenance.source_label: Claude Fable feature idea: spec, extension, and media type
provenance.review_target: Reported 39479-line MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Write the two-page spec, use a .mktctx extension, and define a registered-looking media type such as text/x-mktctx.
feedback.normalized_claim: Publish a compact normative specification and choose stable file-extension and media-type identifiers for discovery and tool integration.

current_behavior: The protocol is taught in a compact in-band guide and described in design notes and examples, but no complete normative grammar and conformance document exists.
The CLI historically writes .txt by default, while format examples also use .txt; .mktctx is not established as the default extension.
No media type is declared or registered.
An x- prefixed media type can be used informally but should not be described as registered without the relevant standards process.

proposal.summary: Create a normative specification with test vectors, then adopt .mktctx and an accurately labeled provisional or registered media type only after compatibility implications are decided.
candidate_changes: Specify grammar, encoding, canonical serialization, framing, identifiers, projections, integrity, errors, extension points, and version compatibility.
Separate normative requirements from explanatory rationale and examples.
Evaluate .mktctx as an explicit-format extension while preserving user-selected .txt output where requested.
Research media-type registration requirements and use standards-accurate language for any provisional identifier.
non_goals: Do not call text/x-mktctx an officially registered media type without registration evidence.
Do not change default output naming or extension without a migration and compatibility decision.
Do not let the short in-band guide substitute for normative byte and failure semantics.

questions: Should .mktctx identify every protocol version or only the current family?
Is the payload always valid text for media-type purposes once encoding policy is decided?
Which portions can fit in a concise core spec and which require extension documents?
risks: Premature ecosystem identifiers can freeze unstable semantics.
Changing the familiar .txt default may break scripts or user expectations.
An incomplete normative spec can create incompatible implementations.
evidence_needed: A complete grammar and conformance test suite.
Audit of current scripts, docs, fixtures, and installer examples that assume .txt.
Standards research for appropriate media-type registration or provisional use.
